questions.q: Which is a valid way to get non-Salesforce data into CRM Analytics?
options: Only by retyping it into a report
Through external connections in Data Manager, CSV upload, the External Data API, or Data 360
Only through Salesforce record sharing
External data cannot be used in CRM Analytics
questions.explain: The lesson covers connections, uploads, the External Data API, and Data 360 as the main routes; availability varies by org and license.

A report type in Lightning Experience
The current name of the product formerly called Data Cloud
A CSV file format
questions.explain: Salesforce renamed Data Cloud to Data 360, though some Trailhead screens still show the older name.

questions.q: Why should a recipe be scheduled to run after its connection sync completes?
options: Recipes cannot run before midnight
Because syncs delete recipes
Because connections require recipes to be disabled
Otherwise the recipe may process stale data from the previous sync
questions.explain: Ordering the schedule (sync first, recipe second) keeps output datasets aligned with fresh source data.

questions.q: Warehouse rows joined into a CRM Analytics dataset don't have Salesforce owners or sharing rules. What should you use to restrict who sees which rows?
options: A security predicate on the dataset
Nothing, since sharing rules apply automatically
A longer dataset name
The API version number
questions.explain: Sharing rules apply to Salesforce objects; external data needs its own row-level protection, typically a dataset security predicate.

questions.q: A synced dataset is best described as what?
options: The live source system itself
A read-only mirror that is always instantly current
A copy whose origin, owner, and freshness should be tracked
A Salesforce object with sharing rules
questions.explain: Synced datasets are copies refreshed on a schedule, so documenting source and freshness helps when numbers disagree.
